target_claim: The construction (group the cut edges of delta(S) by pairs of connected components Si of G[S] and Tj of G[T]) yields sets Cij each of which is claimed to be a minimal cut (bond); in fact Cij need not even be a cut-set.
source_quote:
Therefore, each non-empty Cij is a minimal cut, and we have expressed C as a disjoint
union of minimal cuts.
test_sketch: Implement the stated construction directly: compute components of G[S] and G[T], form Cij = edges between Si and Tj. Oracle: brute-force bond checker (enumerate all vertex bipartitions of graphs with <= 12 vertices; a set is a bond iff it equals delta(X) for some X with G[X] and G[V\X] both connected, minimality checked by subset enumeration or by the both-sides-connected criterion). Input family: cycles C_{2k} with alternating partition, e.g. C4 with vertices 1,2,3,4 (edges 12,23,34,41), S={1,3}, T={2,4}. The construction outputs four singleton sets {12},{23},{34},{41}; the oracle shows removing any single cycle edge leaves the graph connected, so each Cij fails to be a cut-set, refuting the claim that every non-empty Cij is a minimal cut.
